title: Phase 8's _probePoolerDonation — the mechanised form of story-072 checklist line 1197 — is reachable only under `if (isPreview)`, so the broadcast path never runs it
fingerprintNote: Carried VERBATIM from classified-findings.json; not recomputed by finding-manager.
description: BalancerPoolerV2._psmDonate failures are swallowed by try/catch, so a green index-4 mint transaction is NOT evidence that the donation leg works — the exact failure mode story-072 checklist line 1197 exists to catch. That line is a post-broadcast HUMAN step, is UNTICKED, and story-075's :verify explicitly declines to discharge it (VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:85-86 prints 'STILL A HUMAN STEP ... line 1197'). Nothing in the npm chain enforces that the human step ever happens. Meanwhile Phase 8's _probePoolerDonation performs exactly this assertion and PASSED in this audit's :dry run (BatchDonatedViaPSM=true, DonationSkipped=false, USDC stream buffer delta 2485691) — but Phase 8 is `if (isPreview)` only, so it never runs on the broadcast path. The same preview-only gating is the only thing that exercises BALANCER_ROUTER and SUSDS_IS_FIRST, which are private immutable with no getter and therefore unassertable by Phase 0 or by :verify.
impact: None directly. If BalancerPoolerV2._psmDonate were to fail after the cutover, the try/catch swallows it and the index-4 mint still succeeds — the consequence is that a donation which should have reached the batch minter's nudge pot is skipped. Per this project's standing position, those pots are funded by externally-derived yield on protocol-owned capital, so an under-delivered donation is an allocation/marketing miss, NOT an economic loss and NOT a value leak. The real impact is on DETECTION: the wiring assertions cannot see it, because the wiring is in fact correct, so a fully green `:verify` run coexists with a silently non-donating pooler.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. Precondition: after the cutover, some condition (a BALANCER_ROUTER or SUSDS_IS_FIRST misconfiguration — both `private immutable` with no getter, hence unassertable by Phase 0 or by `:verify` — or a Balancer-side change) makes _psmDonate revert.
2. try/catch swallows the revert. The index-4 mint transaction succeeds and emits DonationSkipped instead of BatchDonatedViaPSM.

3. `:verify` re-runs Phase 7's wiring assertions against live state. Every one passes: the dispatcher is registered, the hook is paired, the donor points at the streamer. Wiring is not the broken thing.

4. The only remaining control is story-072 checklist line 1197 — a post-broadcast HUMAN step, currently UNTICKED, which VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:85-86 explicitly declines to discharge ('STILL A HUMAN STEP … line 1197').
5. If the operator does not perform it, the condition persists undetected. Nothing in the npm chain enforces that it happens.
likelihood: low. The donation leg was empirically exercised GREEN in this session's live-fork `:dry` run against the same commit (BatchDonatedViaPSM=true, DonationSkipped=false, USDC stream-buffer delta 2485691), so the pooler is not broken today. The residual is that no automated gate would notice if it broke.
assumptions: A post-cutover donation failure occurs at all — for which there is currently no evidence.
externalRequirements: Either an operator omission of the manual step, or a Balancer/PSM-side change after the cutover.
evidence: side-effects.json -> events[0], externalCalls[4], leadsResolution[6]. Log: scratchpad/dry.log:282 'pooler: BatchDonatedViaPSM / DonationSkipped: true false'. Source: run() :439 `if (isPreview) _phase8_previewSmokeTests()`; VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:85-86.
justification: Ratified at Low after the Medium case was tested and rejected. The Medium case would be 'protocol function impacted': donations silently stop. It fails on two counts. First, there is no demonstrated impairment — the mechanism was proven working on a live fork at this exact commit, so the finding is about a missing DETECTOR, not a broken function; grading a working path as an impaired one would be overstatement. Second, the thing that would be under-delivered is externally-derived yield onto a protocol-owned pot, which this project does not treat as a value leak in either direction. What makes the finding genuinely reportable — and materially stronger than its class sibling L-04 — is the demonstration that the human step is MECHANIZABLE and ALREADY IMPLEMENTED: _probePoolerDonation performs exactly the assertion line 1197 describes, and it passed. An automatable, already-written, already-passing check was left behind an `if (isPreview)` gate while the acceptance criterion it discharges sits unticked. That is a real control-coverage gap and a genuine story-072 deviation, but its honest weight is Low. Consistency check: run-22 graded L-04 — the same BlockingProbeGatedToPreviewOnly family — as Low, and nothing here justifies departing from that.
recommendation: Add a `promotion-ready:verify-mint` npm key that runs the existing Phase 8 pooler probe in PREVIEW_MODE against LIVE POST-cutover state: prank OWNER, trigger one index-4 mint, and `require` that BatchDonatedViaPSM fired and DonationSkipped did not. It needs no broadcast and no signing, so it chains after `:verify` with the same `&&` discipline, converting line 1197 from an unenforced human step into a fail-closed gate. Until that ships, tick line 1197 explicitly before disconnecting the Ledger. Secondary: expose BALANCER_ROUTER and SUSDS_IS_FIRST via public getters so Phase 0 and `:verify` can assert them at all.

specConformance.criterion: checklist line 1197 — post-broadcast human check: trigger one index-4 mint and assert BatchDonatedViaPSM fired.
specConformance.state: UNTICKED. One of only two unticked rows in a 46-item checklist (44 ticked).
specConformance.deviation: The suite ships without discharging an acceptance criterion it is mechanically capable of discharging, and the story-075 verifier built to close the verification gap explicitly declines this row in its own epilogue.

classSiblingDisclosure: Same family as open ledger entry L-04 (e6f32c47…, Low, open). NOT a duplicate and NOT merged: L-04's probe is a PREFLIGHT that must move EARLIER on the broadcast path (ahead of the Kendu whitelist write); this one is a POST-MINT VERIFICATION that must move LATER, into a post-broadcast read-only leg. Neither fix delivers the other. Flag L-04-23-01 is noted: L-04's own probe ran green this session (sent == received == credited == 1e24), which de-risks L-04 without fixing it — that is L-04's re-weighing at /ledger, not a change to this finding.
